subject: Audit & access log: proof-of-export options and delivery evidence
body:

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request — export windows and proof of delivery for audit logs

Hi Karthik / Lauren,

We're preparing for a regulatory audit (external auditor arrives May 6) and need concrete evidence showing that Finova's audit and access logs were exported and delivered from Redwood for the period 2026-10-01 — 2027-03-31. Two quick asks:

1) What export delivery options can you provide (S3 push, signed download URL, transfer manifest)?
2) For each option, what verifiable evidence can you provide to show the export was completed and unchanged (manifest with checksums, signed timestamps, delivery receipts)?

Also please confirm retention windows for the different log types (audit events vs access logs) on hosted vs dedicated/private deployments, and whether exports include the request_id, client IP, user_id, and precise timestamps. Our auditors want an example export (head of file) and a short description of the export pipeline.

Thanks — if you can reply by EOD today that would be ideal.

Best,
Sofia

Hi Sofia — adding specifics below so you can share with auditors. TL;DR: hosted has shorter default retention but full export path exists for 13 months of audit logs; Dedicated/Private customers can extend retention and we provide signed manifests.

Retention summary (hosted defaults):
- Audit logs (configuration changes, role grants, policy edits): retained for 13 months by default.
- Access logs (token requests, embedding/generation requests): retained 90 days by default in hot storage; 13 months available in archive/export on request.

Export capabilities and evidence:
1) Nearline S3 push (recommended for chain-of-custody):
   - Format: newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) or CSV (customer preference).
   - Includes: event timestamp (RFC3339), request_id, client_ip, user_id, model_id, route, response_status, bytes_in/out.
   - Evidence: manifest.json (file list + sizes + SHA256), S3 server-side event logs, and an optional Redwood-signed delivery PDF (timestamp + manifest hash).

2) Ad-hoc signed URL:
   - One-off URL that expires; includes file-level checksum. Good for quick review but weaker for long-term chain-of-custody.

3) Full archive export:
   - For windows older than 90 days we run an archive job (can cover up to 13 months depending on retention policy). Typical turnaround: 3–5 business days.

4) Deletion confirmation:
   - If you request bulk deletion for a customer scope we provide a signed deletion report listing object keys removed and a deletion-job run ID. (This is different from export evidence.)

Security / encryption:
- Exports to customer S3 support SSE-KMS; we can also perform client-side encryption if you supply a transfer key.

Examples & attachments:
- redwood_export_manifest_example.json — example manifest showing SHA256 and file sizes.
- redwood_log_export_instructions.pdf — describes the export fields and sample request payload to trigger an export.

If the auditor needs the first N rows, we can include a head sample (we included a small CSV sample in the thread). If you want the Redwood-signed confirmation PDF, that is provided as a one-time artifact and requires a short signing request (we'll route to legal/compliance).

Happy to hop on a 15-min call with the auditor if helpful.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Compliance, Redwood Inference

Hi Sofia — Marissa here from deliveries. To move forward we need:
1) S3 bucket ARN + write role ARN (preferred) OR a decision to accept a signed download link.
2) Desired time range confirmed: you asked 2026-10-01 — 2027-03-31, please reconfirm.
3) Preferred export format (JSONL or CSV) and whether you want the Redwood-signed confirmation PDF.

Estimated delivery windows once we have access:
- Nearline export (last 90 days): ~48 hours (we create the manifest, push to S3, and provide the manifest and delivery proof).
- Archive export (up to 13 months back): 3–5 business days. If there are additional retention tiers beyond 13 months we can discuss legal/archival retrieval but that is an extra-cost engagement.

I've attached the Finova schema we prefer to use for the S3 delivery (finova_s3_export_schema.csv) and a blank export delivery proof template you can use for the auditor (export_delivery_proof_template.docx). Please send the S3 details and I'll kick off the job immediately.

Thanks,
